hypothesis: A legacy 22-character or standard 30-character Bitcoin minikey may occur inside an already recorded clue-based reading, rather than occupying the entire reading.

selector.directions: All existing down/up and normal/character_reverse variants matching those fields; no new variants generated.

deduplication: Unique recorded candidate text, then unique resulting form text, then unique shape-compatible minikey value. Preserve every source locator.
formatRule: Exactly uppercase S followed by Base58 characters; SHA256 of ASCII candidate plus question mark must start with byte 00.
secretDerivation: For format-valid minikeys only, one SHA256 of the exact ASCII candidate, as specified by the minikey format. No arbitrary text hashing.
activityChecks: Only if a format-valid minikey exists. Read-only Blockstream Esplora address statistics, with successful zero-activity outcomes independently checked via mempool.space; failures remain failures. Controls never queried. No cache reuse.
successCriterion: A format-valid candidate is only a follow-up lead. A reproducible reading with activity requires private review and corroboration; no automatic claim that it is Max Keiser’s prize.
negativeCriterion: If no minikey passes the formatcheck, exclude literal22/30 minikeys within these exact 42 forms. If valid minikeys exist but all declared derived addresses have successfully verified zero confirmed/mempooltransactions, exclude those concrete key/address interpretations at the recorded check time.
inconclusiveCriterion: Scope/hash/control failure or any unresolved address lookup failure prevents a complete negative activity result.
stopRule: No extra lengths, case changes, substitutions, punctuation deletion, padding, salts, repeated hashes, alternate encodings, extra address indices or post-hoc transformations in this run. New ideas require a new protocol.

sources.use: Alternate complete printed lines and first-word reading; applicability to this specific issue remains inferred.
Standard 30/legacy 22 character format, 8-bit typo check, defined SHA256 secret conversion.

limitations: This is a validator coverage correction, not a new independent cipher family.
First-word initials and mirror variants are inherited hypotheses; the creator did not specify minikey format.
The minikey check has only 8 bits; chance passes are expected in sufficiently large shape-compatible sets.
No authenticated prize address is known; inactive addresses do not exclude other encodings or derivation schemes.
Other subsets of the 2,034 recorded streams, including manually annotated bold selections, are outside this tight audit.
publication: Register protocol and implementation before scanning; preserve original20261109files unchanged. Do not publish an operational secret or candidate locators if activity requires review.
candidateFingerprint: SHA256 of ASCII domain KEY404/minikey-window-audit/fingerprint/v1 followed by NUL and the exact candidate. A plain SHA256(candidate) would be its private scalar and must not be published.
